narrative:
The model predicts you have a 21% chance of failing your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this prediction were your lack of desire to pursue higher education, your clean record of zero past failures, and the fact that your father is your guardian. Surprisingly, your intention not to continue studying after this year was the single biggest reason the model leaned toward failure. Because nearly every student who passes expresses a clear wish to go on to higher education, your answer stood out as a strong warning signal. Your perfect record of no previous failures actually pushed the prediction in the opposite direction, slightly favoring a pass, since students who succeed also tend to have no prior failures. Having your father as guardian likewise nudged the outcome mildly toward passing, though this effect was smaller.

In short, the model sees your stated lack of interest in further education as the dominant factor outweighing the protective influence of your clean academic history and family situation.

To improve, you should seriously reflect on your future goals. If you can reconnect with a reason to aim higher—whether through career talks, exploring subjects that excite you, or speaking with a counselor—you may find the motivation that currently seems missing. Taking the remedial courses seriously could also help rebuild that sense of direction before it is too late.
